audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Gnar five of seven stages at 2/10 in a lane Tryndamere wins 51.6% of, and rows 2, 4 and 6 disagree with the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: The mirrored gnar__tryndamere audit set win[2]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[6]=Tryndamere with matching phases sides. Level 3 is genuinely even (your E threat against his ranged poke) and two items on favours the split-pusher over a champion who needs Mega form and a teamfight to matter.
audit.corrected: Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere — rows 2, 4 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on any spike, and the Mega-form spike was framed as an unconditional lane flip.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s (reduced when caught on the return), Wallop 7s, Hop/Crunch 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, GNAR! 90/60/30s. Mega form is not a state he holds — Rage builds only in combat.
audit.corrected: Spikes now carry the real numbers and the Rage condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: GNAR! was described as a stun everywhere on the page. It only stuns enemies thrown into a wall.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Mega Gnar throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' In open ground it is a displacement plus slow — no stun. This is the decisive positional rule of the matchup and it was absent from all fifteen report sections.
audit.corrected: GNAR! only stuns enemies it throws into a wall — fight in open ground and it is just a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout appeared nowhere, and the page's kiting advice invites exactly the mistake it punishes.
audit.why: Mocking Shout cuts attack damage in an 850 area on 14s, but its movement slow applies only to enemies with their backs turned. Turning to run from Gnar is what makes it work against you, not for you.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout only slows a target whose back is turned — leave facing him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Boomerang Throw's catch-refund was never stated.
audit.why: 'If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced' — standing so the return path does not pass through him is a free way to hold him to the full 16s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Stand off the return line and his Q stays on its full cooldown.

edits.before: At level 6 mini Gnar has no escape, so your E plus R Undying Rage all-in favors you.
edits.after: At 6 your R all-in beats mini form, but if his rage bar fills Mega flips it back.

edits.before: With two-plus items Mega Gnar's CC and durability wall you off the fight, favoring him.
edits.after: With two-plus items your crit split-push beats a Gnar who must group to matter.

edits.before: Once you have E Spinning Slash you can commit to a Q Bloodlust-fueled all-in, but Gnar's boomerang Q and Hyper-empowered autos out-poke you at range, so pick your window when his Q is down.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1, but catching it on the return cuts that cooldown hard — stand so the boomerang cannot come back through him, and commit in the gap while it is still travelling.

edits.before: The moment Gnar hits Mega form he flips the lane — GNAR! stun into E-W knockback plus Botrk/Steraks armor lets him body you even through R, so respect his rage bar.
edits.after: Mega Gnar's Wallop is a 7s stun and Crunch is a 22s leap at rank 1 — that is the pair to bait. GNAR! itself only stuns if a wall is behind you, so hold open ground.

edits.before: Mega Gnar in a teamfight walls you off and CCs you out of the carry — you must split away from his rage windows and only dive when his transform is on cooldown.
edits.after: Mega form is a teamfight tool, so take the map away from it: his Rage only builds in combat, and a Gnar farming a side lane arrives as Mini. Split where he must answer alone.

edits.before: Once Gnar reaches Mega form and picks up Botrk/Steraks the matchup inverts — his GNAR! stun and E-W knockback can peel you off even through your ult, so play the sidelane around his transform cooldown and avoid his rage windows.
edits.after: Mega Gnar's GNAR! only stuns what it throws into a wall, so fight him in open ground and it is a slow, not a stun. Rage builds only in combat — disengage and he drops back to Mini. Side-lane him where no wall is behind you.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. R survives it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - GNAR! (R): 90s at rank 1 — it only stuns if a wall is behind you. - Boomerang Throw (Q): 16s, far less if he catches the return. - Crunch/Hop (E): 22s at rank 1, his only escape.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. R survives it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 and needs a wall behind you to stun. Deny both.

edits.before: That is Gnar's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows a target whose back is turned — leave facing him.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. R survives it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: GNAR! only stuns enemies it throws into a wall — fight in open ground and it is just a slow.

notes: Left alone: diff is 'EVEN' but tone is '#ff5d6c' (the hard-lane red) and diffRating is 8.5/10, in a lane won 51.6%. The three fields contradict each other; I did not guess the EVEN tone hex. Also unchanged: Gnar's E carries a 'terrain' flag in the kit — Riot's text describes a leap that bounces off units, creating no terrain, so I did not write it. His R's terrain flag is correct in effect (walls are what make it stun) and I used that.
